summary: API Gateway priority-skip misroute causing sudden 5xx amplification for LensForge
description: Issue summary: LensForge started reporting a rapid increase in 5xx responses on their production routes beginning 2026-03-10 11:08 UTC. Impact: multiple customer endpoints returned 502/503/504 for short-lived bursts, causing retries from their client and amplified traffic. Environment: prod us-east (customer pinned to dedicated cluster), traffic pattern: a mix of long-context generation and streaming chat. Steps to reproduce: 1) Simulate mixed long-prompt (>4k tokens) and short-prompt traffic at LensForge tenant rate; 2) Ensure priority headers set to 'low' for diagnostic clients; 3) Observe gateway routing decisions and upstream failures. Observed behavior: api-gateway bypassed usual backpressure path for a subset of connections (priority-skip), sending long-prompt requests directly to the hottest runtime pool which began exhibiting OOM and watchdog restarts. Expected behavior: gateway should apply priority-shed/backpressure and route to fallback or queue rather than hot-pool overload. Logs & metrics: abrupt kernel swap and OOM traces on runtime hosts, apigw accept-queue spike, keepalive churn, and queue fairness metric collapse. Temporary mitigation: rate-limited LensForge tenant at edge and enabled fallback-to-quantized-model in routing policy to reduce GPU memory usage.

investigation_notes: Initial analysis indicates a configuration regression in the ingress prioritizer that allowed certain connections to bypass the backpressure path when a metadata tag 'experimental-route-skip' was present. This caused the API gateway to forward heavy long-context requests into a runtime hot-pool already near memory capacity. Runtimes responded with OOM kills and watchdog restarts, producing 502/503 and occasional 504 during connection teardown. Correlated metrics: apigw accept_queue_length +400% at peak, runtime GPU memory usage hitting 99%, kernel fallback logs spiking, and kv-cache latency doubling. We confirmed request ids from customer traces mapped to the same runtime node group. Affected code paths: apigw prioritizer evaluation and routing skip predicate. Temporary mitigation validated: tenant rate-limit + fallback-to-quantized-model reduced downstream OOM occurrences.
resolution: Hotfix applied to apigw prioritizer to remove 'skip' behavior and enforce backpressure gating (apigw PR 1290). Runtime pods restarted with quantized fallback and updated autoscaler thresholds to scale earlier. Customer LensForge was rate-limited during remediation window; rate limits lifted after stability confirmed. No data loss; retries were client-side. Incident classified as Sev1; customer SLAs met via expedited response and communication. Follow-up items assigned for autoscaler tuning and integration tests.
follow_up_actions: Create integration test that simulates mixed long/short prompt priority traffic (owner: eng/runtime)
Add telemetry metric for 'priority-skip' counts and alert when >10/min (owner: apigw)
Tune autoscaler GPU usage threshold to begin scale at 80% rather than 92% for dedicated clusters (owner: infra/autoscaler)
Perform postmortem and share with LensForge and internal teams (owner: SRE)
Audit tenant metadata parsing to avoid experimental flags being present in prod routing policies (owner: security)
